newsitem.title: POLAND: STALEXPORT SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE ISSUE FOR EBRD.
newsitem.headline: STALEXPORT SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE ISSUE FOR EBRD.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish steel trader Stalexport SA voted on Saturday to issue one million to four million shares to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the company said.

It said in a statement that a general shareholders' meeting decided to increase the company's share capital by between 10 million and 40 million zlotys through an issue of "D" series shares worth a nominal 10 zlotys each.
"The issue...will be designated for a closed share issue directed to the EBRD," the stateent said.
The shareholders authorised the management to set the issue's price, after consulting the board of directors, as well as the dates and other details of the issue.
The issue price would not be lower than the arithmetical average price of the 30 consecutive sessions beginning from the 45th session before the issue's opening date.
The issue would carry dividend rights from January 1, 1997, it said.

Earlier this month Stalexport spokesman Jacek Czeladko told Reuters that the EBRD had shown interest in buying shares worth $20 million to $25 million, adding that the bank's holding would boost the firm's prestige.
Czeladko said the EBRD would buy the shares at no lower than 36.5 zlotys and that the price could increase depending on Stalexport's bourse performance in the coming weeks.
Czeladko said the EBRD could initially approve the deal in June or July, allowing for an issue in September or October.
He said that as part of the deal the EBRD would also lend Stalexport another $20 million to $25 million over five to seven years.
Funds from the issue and loans would go toward buying firms which collect and process scrap metal. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
